category_title: Highly reserved and anxious students with significant writing avoidance
minimal_context: The teacher is conducting a writing conference with Shelly during writing workshop.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Shelly, let's continue our writing conference. What is the next part of your draft?

STUDENT: I have a story about a butterfly.

TUTOR: Please remember the rule, don't interrupt during conferences.

STUDENT: But I want to tell you my butterfly story right now.

TUTOR: You need to go back to your seat and wait until I am finished.

STUDENT: (Interrupting the writing conference again) It was a really big butterfly and it flew all the way up into the sky!

options.A: Joke with the student about the interruption and laugh at oneself during the writing conference.
options.B: Draw a page in the air, pretend to write the butterfly story, and drink an imaginary cappuccino.
options.C: Prioritize the student's social-emotional need for connection over strict rule enforcement; validate the student's idea immediately.
options.D: Accurately model the correct pronunciation of the words the student used to describe the butterfly.
